whatIsIt.eli5: The photo you give the model, made square and turned into three layers of numbers: red, green and blue.
whatIsIt.simple: The image is resized (keeping its shape, with grey padding) to a square such as 640×640 and stored as 3 channels of numbers between 0 and 1.
whatIsIt.engineer: Letterboxed RGB tensor 3×H×W, values scaled to [0, 1]; H = W = imgsz (multiple of the max stride, 32).

whyExists.eli5: The model can only read numbers, and it needs every photo to be the same size.
whyExists.simple: A fixed square size lets the network run on batches and makes every stride-2 step divide evenly. The size must be a multiple of 32 (the largest stride).
whyExists.engineer: Batched inference requires fixed shapes; imgsz % max_stride == 0 so every level has an integer grid.

eli5: Make the photo fit a square.
Turn each pixel into three numbers.
simple: Resize so the long side equals the input size, keep the aspect ratio.
Pad the short side with grey (letterbox).
engineer: Larger imgsz raises small-object recall and cost roughly quadratically (FLOPs ∝ H·W).

tradeoffs.eli5: A bigger photo shows tiny weeds better but is slower.
tradeoffs.simple: Doubling the input size makes every map 4× bigger, so compute grows about 4×. For tiny objects in drone photos, a larger input (or tiling) often matters more than any block change.
tradeoffs.engineer: FLOPs scale ~(imgsz/640)²; small-object AP is very sensitive to input resolution.
